There’s more to a Pilgrim
Welcome to a truly special prep school
I loved my time at Pilgrims'. I enjoyed everything; the music, the sport, my friends - and the teachers prepared me really well for senior school.
A warm welcome from the Headmaster: Tim Butcher
I attended Pilgrims’ as a boy. I came back as a teacher and I now have the privilege of being the Headmaster. Like I did, boys arrive at a young age still finding their way in the world and experiencing a great many things for the first time. Up to nine years later they leave with confidence and character, knowing they are ready for what is next because they have been stretched through a culture of personalised expectations. This is what we are about.
Discover THE Pilgrims’ School
We believe Pilgrims’ offers boys the best start in life at the most crucial time in their development. Our boys work hard and have a lot of fun. Our ‘super curriculum’ offers opportunities unique anywhere at Prep School level and designed to appeal to a boy’s curiosity.
With nearly a century of experience, we’re experts in building boys of good character who enjoy learning, love general knowledge and leave ready to make the world a better place.
We encourage every boy to explore his individual ideas and creativity, something they develop as they move up the school. With numerous music ensembles, multiple choirs, all the sports you can think of and more, up to 50 extra-curricular activities a week, strong drama and LAMDA opportunities, and boarding, we’re a one-stop shop for a comprehensive curriculum, afterschool clubs and wrap-around care combined.
Boarding
Boarding at Pilgrims’ is a truly enriching experience with a great sense of fun and community. We have 100 boarding places, and boys can board from Year 4 onwards.
Creative & Performing Arts
In Pre-Prep, music and creativity are at the heart of daily life, helping boys explore, express themselves, and build confidence through play, song, and imaginative activities.

Location
A truly idyllic location: an hour from London by direct train, between Winchester College and Winchester Cathedral, surrounded by the countryside of the South Downs National Park.

HEADMASTER’S WELCOME
Be part of something special
A warm welcome from the Headmaster: Tim Butcher
I attended Pilgrims’ as a boy. I came back as a teacher and I now have the privilege of being the Headmaster. Like I did, boys arrive at a young age still finding their way in the world and experiencing a great many things for the first time. Up to nine years later they leave with confidence and character, knowing they are ready for what is next because they have been stretched through a culture of personalised expectations. This is what we are about. Not producing specialists, honing just a single talent and building everything else around it. The boy who performs in the drama production on one day is debating a point in the classroom the next. The boy who sings a solo in the cathedral on Thursday runs out with the 1st XV on Saturday. A leaver may not be sure if they are ready yet, which is a more useful educational outcome than feeling they’re right. The captain serves. The singer leads. We don’t ask boys to choose between these things because we don’t think they should have to. Our aim is to send boys into the world who are, in the best sense, impossible to summarise. Interested in the world around them and interesting to the people they meet – a rare combination with unmeasured value.
None of this works without the people around the boys here. Pilgrims’ is a genuinely warm community, and that isn’t incidental to our ambition for the boys, it’s what makes it possible. Boys here look out for one another. They form friendships that last well beyond Year 8. They leave knowing how to be a good person in a room, and in a team. These are things that no exam can measure and that no school should stop trying to teach.
Our setting in Winchester is part of this in ways that are hard to separate out. The cathedral, the College chapel, the medieval Pilgrims’ Hall are not just a backdrop. They are a daily presence in boys’ lives, in bringing a sense of something that matters beyond the individual, in the music, in the specific confidence that comes from performing in a space before you’re old enough to be overawed by it. Our relationship with Winchester College stretches that further still, opening up resources, learning opportunities and experiences that very few prep schools can offer. Boys leave Pilgrims’ for a wide range of excellent senior schools. We have a strong scholarship record and we’re proud of it. But we’re equally proud of all the boys who walk into their next school with a sense of self, a love of learning and primed for what’s next.
There’s more to a Pilgrim. Please do come and visit us to find out for yourself – a very warm welcome awaits.
Tim Butcher, Headmaster

Aims, Purpose and Values
There’s more to a Pilgrim
Interesting and interested. That’s a Pilgrim.
We suit boys who make the most of the opportunities we offer and contribute to the school community. While founded on a Christian ethos, we welcome boys of all faiths and none and we aim to foster the character of every single Pilgrim.
Whether day or boarding, we nurture each boy’s interests and help him meet his full potential.
We value character alongside academic results. Our pupils might be playing in an orchestra one day or acting in a play, then on the sports field covered in mud the next. We don’t ask boys to choose. It’s all about AND at Pilgrims’.
Giving boys lots to do, in a whole host of activities, our dedicated staff nurture every individual. We combine this with outstanding facilities and an ethos which values kindness – all in a unique town and country historic setting.
An absolute gem for boys to be themselves whilst flourishing and achieving beyond their potential.
Our aims
There really is more to a Pilgrims’ boy.
We encourage each of them:
to develop confidence tempered with humility;
to appreciate beauty and to be creative;
to value and develop his faith;

Pilgrims’ Parley
Thought provoking discussion with educational experts
The Pilgrims’ Parley is our thought-provoking discussion series, bringing together leading voices from education and beyond to explore important questions affecting children, schools and wider society. Led by Headmaster Tim Butcher, with three a year, each Parley encourages informed debate, diverse perspectives and meaningful conversation on contemporary issues in education and child development.

About us
An exceptional Prep School for boys aged 4-13
The genuine warmth shown by the teachers towards not just our son, but towards us as parents as well, is palpable and quite unique.
Town and Country
An ancient flint wall forms the boundary to our games pitches; next to school, the Bishop’s Palace and the ruins of Wolvesey Castle. They really are in a league of their own.
Few school pitches offer such a setting. We use Winchester College’s grounds and facilities too, effectively extending our campus over the road and giving boys an impressive theatre, sports centre, museum (The Treasury) observatory and even more sports pitches.
A tributary of the River Itchen flows through our grounds. Further downstream the boys can learn to fish and the nearby water meadows, made famous by Keats, are classed as a SSI or Site of Special Scientific Interest, because of the rare habitat they provide for wildlife. An Iron Age fort with a maze at the top of St Catherine’s Hill is within easy walking distance. This setting is a resource in itself, perfect for supervised adventures which inspire a love of learning.
Ancient Roots
Before The Pilgrims’ School, even older institutions played a part in educating boys in Winchester, with various educational establishments here since Saxon times. A school for boys who sang in Winchester Cathedral’s Choir can be traced to the Alta Schola, established around 676AD. Our main school building was redesigned in the 17th century but sits on Roman and medieval constructions. The Pilgrims’ Hall, which we use every day for assemblies, music practices and performances, is one of the oldest buildings in Winchester. It’s so well preserved, visitors come from all over the world to see its magnificent hammer-beam roof, most likely constructed in the first half of the 14th century.
The school moved to its current site in 1931. It became a Winchester school for non-choristers as well as the choristers. We’re now a forward-thinking prep school, proud of this heritage and looking forward to our centenary.
In 1966, the Quiristers of Winchester College Chapel Choir joined Pilgrims’ and they remain of course today. Our Pre-Prep opened in 2007.
Inspiring & Idyllic
We are blessed with a unique location. An hour from London by train, with easy access to Heathrow, Gatwick and Southampton airports but with the English countryside on our doorstep.
The school sits between Winchester College and Winchester Cathedral, in the secure and secluded Cathedral Close with grounds extending into the flint ruins of Wolvesey Castle.
Being in the heart of a vibrant city like Winchester means cafés, shops, theatres and a cinema on our doorstep, but step out of our back gate and you’ll find the water meadows, wildlife and the South Downs Way.

“I love everything about teaching at The Pilgrims’ School. It is a very special place. I feel very lucky to be working with such wonderful boys and staff, with the added bonus of a beautiful setting.”
Tim Butcher
Headmaster / DDSL (Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead)
Tim Butcher
Headmaster / DDSL (Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead)
Now here in my third guise at Pilgrims', I originally left as a boy with a love of pretty much everything... I have continued sport, music and drama in different ways over the years. Through much of my early teaching career I managed to keep involved with semi-professional singing and have had a habit of spending past school holidays leading music theatre camps, workshops and productions for children, or gathering old friends together to put on carol concerts.
I'm a Dad to three lovely children and we all enjoy the Great Outdoors. From the wonder of Northumberland's coast and castles, to the ruggedness of western Wales and Snowdonia, from beaches to mountains and lakes, we get out when we can, enjoying the simple things in life. According to my children, I'm in my element hiking up 'big hills' to look at 'old stones'.
Matt Sutherland
English Teacher / Head of Boarding
Matt Sutherland
English Teacher / Head of Boarding
I am now in my 15th year of teaching, and I am delighted to be joining Pilgrims' this year. Prior to entering the teaching profession, I spent a number of years as an Army Officer and prior to that I followed my degree into field archaeology, working both in the UK and internationally.
When not in the classroom or on the sports pitches, I am responsible for the running of the boarding provision at Pilgrims', building on my experience of boarding in a school setting as well as in the care and training of young people taking their first steps in Army life (much like school boarding but with rather more firearms).
I am married and live at Pilgrims' with my wife and three children - two of whom also attend the school. In our spare time, we like to swap arguing at home for long walks and arguing at historical sites instead. I enjoy art and music, being competent at drums and questionable at guitar. I also enjoy gardening and DIY - a risky interest when living in a historic listed building.
Sarah Hall
Head of Pre-Prep / DDSL (Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead)
Sarah Hall
Head of Pre-Prep / DDSL (Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead)
With nearly 30 years of teaching experience, I’ve had the privilege of guiding and nurturing young minds throughout my career. I began teaching at a Cathedral school in Devon and have since taught in various settings, both state and independent. This breadth of experience has equipped me with a deep understanding of different educational contexts. I am passionate about working with the Pre-Prep boys here at Pilgrims’, helping to cultivate their curiosity and confidence during these formative years. My approach to teaching is rooted in creating a nurturing, engaging environment where each child feels valued and inspired to learn.
Outside of school, I live by the sea, which has become a source of relaxation and creativity for me. One of my greatest passions is searching for sea glass along the shore and transforming these treasures into art. This hobby allows me to blend my love for nature with my artistic side. In my free time, I cherish walks with my husband, children, and our dog, exploring the coast and appreciating the simple beauty of the sea. Being married to a musician, I’ve been fortunate to experience world-class music in some of the UK’s most iconic venues, enjoying a host of incredible musical events. When I’m in my school office, listening to the ensembles rehearsing, it truly is music to my ears! I also enjoy going to the theatre, watching both plays and musicals, which further enriches my love for the arts.
Whether I’m teaching in the classroom or combing the beach for mermaid treasure, I’m continually inspired by the world around me and enjoy bringing that sense of wonder into my work with the boys here at Pilgrims'.
Emma Short
Registrar and PE Teacher
Emma Short
Registrar and PE Teacher
I joined Pilgrims’ having been Head of Sport at my previous school. I now look after Admissions, helping new parents joining the school. Lucky for me I still get the chance to teach sport.
I love all things water based and can often be found paddle boarding along the Dorset coast or hiking with husband, Andrew, and our three boys, all former Pilgrims'.

Chaplaincy & Faith
‘He Who Would Valiant Be…’
CHAPLAINCY & FAITH
Founded as the choir school of Winchester Cathedral, we are a Church of England school where Christian values form the guiding principles for our values and relationships. All boys are welcome, regardless of cultural backgrounds or faith, and we encourage and support them to follow their own conscience in matters of religion and faith.
We have a Lay Chaplain who helps to coordinate the faith aspects of the school’s life and who is always available to support boys with these. Winchester Cathedral is our chapel. Several of our services are celebrated in its magnificent nave and Quire, the most memorable possibly being our carol service which allows us to mark both the end of the Christmas term and the exciting time that is yet to come with family.
Each week there are three school assemblies, allowing for different focal points and emphases, supported by colleagues from both the cathedral and College chaplaincy teams. We also have a short reflection period at the end of a Thursday. On Sundays, boarders are able to attend Eucharist in the Cathedral or a religious service elsewhere, with particular provision for Catholic families through Winchester College.
In the Lent term, Senior boys are invited to consider if they would like to be confirmed. The confirmation service is held in the Cathedral and candidates are supported by the whole school, their families, and friends. As preparation for their confirmation, boys meet weekly to explore the meaning of spirituality and their personal response to their faith with a member of clergy. Confirmation classes are informal and usually involve chocolate.
The spiritual development of the pupils is excellent. Pupils are inspired both by the all-pervading spirituality of the historic environment and by the soul-inspiring and uplifting music, which permeate and enrich every aspect of life for the whole community. This is a strength of the school.

Home > The Educational Journey > Prep School (7-13 yrs) > Prep Curriculum > Performing Arts
PERFORMING ARTS
Because all the world’s a stage
PERFORMING ARTS
Drama might look like simply playing a part, but it’s all about human connections. It’s a great way to learn about emotions and feelings. Speaking confidently, working as a team, or communicating with a sense of conviction and compassion – drama is key to developing self-confidence.
Boys have many opportunities to perform, from public speaking and LAMDA competitions to workshops, readings and large-scale productions. Every boy gets involved, on stage or behind the scenes, helping to build confidence and creativity.
Drama lessons often follow themes such as Greek Theatre, Shakespeare or our recent double bill of Agatha Christie where accents, movement and improvisation came into play. Collaborative work encourages boys to express themselves and become articulate performers. We also have several professional theatres nearby with their own productions as well as receiving hit West End tours.
There’s a real focus on a fully rounded education for the boys. There’s not just music, not just sport and not just academic focus – it’s really everything. And that’s important.
LAMDA
The London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art (LAMDA) is one of the country’s top drama schools and an awarding body for Performance and Communication exams.
Taking LAMDA exams in Acting and Verse & Prose develops transferable life skills, encourages friendships, and overall, is a lot of fun.
We have a 100% pass rate and excellent results, but the main benefit is seeing boys grow in self-confidence.
PILGRIMS’ GOT TALENT

MUSIC
Our ISI Inspection (2026) recognised music as a ‘significant strength’
MUSIC & SINGING
Music is everywhere at Pilgrims’. Even if boys don’t play an instrument or sing in one of our choirs, they feel the benefit. We inspire an understanding and appreciation of music which boys find invaluable for the rest of their lives.
From Reception to Year 8, all boys have timetabled class music lessons. We aim to equip each boy with the tools to unlock a deeper understanding of the subject, irrespective of his musical ability.
Neuroscience shows the benefits of music and singing both in terms of inspiring creativity and as a stimulus for brain development.
The Pilgrims’ School Music Showreel – 2025 – YouTube
A unique 'double-choir' school in which almost every boy both sings and learns an instrument - Tatler Schools Guide
LEARNING AN INSTRUMENT
Not surprisingly, there are more instrumental lessons each week than there are boys in the school.
A dedicated team of 28 specialist visiting music teachers means boys can learn any orchestral instrument, in addition to piano, organ, guitar, flute and of course, their voice. Music lessons are arranged so that disruption to lessons is kept to a minimum, ensuring that we preserve the balance between academic subjects, sport, music and free time.
Music practice rooms, including a sound-proofed suite with recording facilities, are mostly located in the music block, but there are pianos, including four grands, dotted all around the school.
Boarders also have timetabled practising slots supervised by the music staff.
MUSICAL ENSEMBLES & PERFORMANCE OPPORTUNITIES
Practising in isolation is one thing, but the stimulus of group music-making is key to a successful musician – it’s also much more fun!
Performing starts in Pre-Prep and, from Year 6 onwards, two-thirds of boys play in ensembles. Boys perform in at least 12 concerts each year, ranging from the formal to the extremely informal. Chamber music is greatly encouraged and music is specially arranged for any ad hoc combinations that may arise when friends decide to pool their resources. The orchestra plays repertoire that one might expect to hear at a senior school.
Ensemble opportunities include, the Jazz Band, the Rock band, Orchestra and Strings, Guitar, Recorder, Woodwind and Baroque Ensembles, as well as Big Band and Orchestra.
The Chamber Choir Tour to Sorrento, that was really memorable. I met lots of lovely people and it really strengthened the bonds within the choir too. That would probably be my favourite memory, but there were so many, it's very hard to choose.
MUSIC EXAMS & SCHOLARSHIPS
Forgive us if we blow our own trumpet…
Graded music exam results for Pilgrims’ boys are consistently high. Most awarded are distinctions or high merits. Many boys attain Grade 5+ each year and pass their Grade 5 theory.
While grades, depth and breadth of repertoire are important, our aim is enjoyment.
We have an enviable record in securing music awards to senior schools, and a significant number of Pilgrims go on to read music at university, many as a choral scholar at either Oxford or Cambridge.
CHOIRS in addition to our CHORISTERS
We know singing is good for us. You’ll hear snatches of song at all times of day.
We have four school choirs including the Chamber Choir who sing for the Christmas Lights switch on every year in Winchester and other high profile events.
The composer, Stephen Barton, a former Pilgrim and Chorister, says
‘Pilgrims’ is a specialist music school in all but title with the finest prep school music department in the country’.
Stephen works regularly with our Choristers on commercial recordings. Our Choristers and Quiristers make up a total of 38 pupils at Pilgrims’.
Winchester is known across the world as a centre of choral excellence and all our Choristers receive what is arguably the best music education in the world.

CREATIVE ARTS
Our setting inspires creativity in all its forms.
ART
We have a wonderful light-filled art studio that’s always buzzing with creativity. Boys are encouraged to explore and experiment with a wide range of media. From watercolours and detailed line drawings to pottery, printmaking and photography, the art curriculum at Pilgrims’ builds confidence and allows every boy to develop his own unique artistic voice. We study a diverse range of artists and makers from all over the world and use their work to inspire and inform our own practice and projects. There are many opportunities for boys to practise art and develop independence and freedom to explore during activity time and commoners. Boys enjoy the art studio as a calm and relaxed space to be creative in their spare time and enjoy extending their own areas of artistic interest e.g. painting, animation, sculpture, illustration and digital art.
A message from Ros Priddle
Head of Art
It’s a dream come true working at Pilgrims’. Our imaginations run wild in the art studio.
It’s a large creative space and I love seeing the boys’ ideas come to life.
For me art is about so much more than teaching drawing, painting or how to make a sculpture. It’s about opening young minds to the world around them and helping our Pilgrims’ express themselves. In terms of development and wellbeing, art provides an essential outlet for boys’ emotions growing up and it’s a privilege to help guide them along the way.
DESIGN & TECHNOLOGY
A Message from Amy Herbert
Head of Design & Technology
Design and technology is the subject where mathematical brainboxes and science whizzkids turn their bright ideas into useful products. James Dyson
IT AND DIGITAL LEARNING
While we keep screen time to a minimum, IT has an important role in education as in the real world.
Our two IT suites have state-of-the-art tech and there’s cross over between what’s taught here and other subjects. Boys enjoy programming robotic models, designing their own games, coding and making films. We also use drones and robots so that the boys can see physical outcomes to their coding. Boys’ learning is enriched with programming in various computer languages, AI and stop-frame animation.
Purple Mash is a platform used by the younger boys to get deeper into their coding journey. Our dancing robot, Polly Pilgrim, offers a different way to code, as well as being good fun to watch.
Further up the school, the boys’ learning is enriched with programming in various computer languages, stop-frame animation, and game creation, as well as making sure they are comfortable with Microsoft Office and editing software. Virtual reality headsets have been very successful in bringing subjects to life through a fully immersive experience. Returning from a visit to the Tutankhamun exhibition, Year 3 put on the VR headsets to find themselves standing in the entrance to an Egyptian tomb. The sense of having been there greatly enhanced the boys’ articles, written for The Daily Hieroglyph after their visit.
Message from Jake Reynolds
Head of Digital Learning
We have a no phones in school policy day to day but there’s no escaping the need for young people to grow up able to understand and use all the tech around us. It means school plays a crucial role in keeping that balance.
You’d be forgiven for thinking my classes are all in, well, the classroom, but far from it. You’re just as likely to see me taking a class in the Quad, coding then racing robots, or filming, before going back inside to edit rushes or create animations.
The world we live in requires a measured response to the technological advances happening day to day, so we take pride in being across it all so we can guide the boy to use digital technology in a positive way.

ENGLISH
THE ENGLISH CURRICULUM
Pilgrims' is an absolutely fantastic school with the most incredible and dedicated teachers. My son is nurtured and encouraged, in all the right amounts. The staff really understand my son and genuinely really care.
ENRICHMENT FOR ENGLISH
Enrichment at Pilgrims’ brings learning to life through theatre trips, author visits and workshops that inspire creativity and insight into the writer’s craft.
Speaking and listening skills are developed through classroom discussion, debate and opportunities to speak in assemblies and services at Winchester Cathedral and Winchester College Chapel, with senior boys also gaining confidence through guiding visitors around the school.
ACCELERATED READER
Accelerated Reader (AR) is a system that helps monitor boys’ independent reading. Pilgrims’ can pick a book at their own level and read it at their own pace. When they have finished, they take a short quiz. AR gives the boys and teachers feedback based to help with what they might want to read next. AR has over 30,000 books on record with quizzes for each, and more are being added every day.
AR keeps a running total of all the words each boy has read. Keeping track of this ‘Word Count’ is something that strongly motivates the boys – the goal is for a boy to become a ‘Word Millionaire’ during an academic year.
BRIGGS LIBRARY
Reading is at the core of the Pilgrims’ way of life, so the library is always open. Boys use it in lessons, breaks, before and after the school or just as somewhere homely to sit quietly and read. Magazines and newspapers are available too with chess sets and comfy sofas.
Our impressive collection of fiction includes the classics alongside the latest releases, while the reference section aims to support the curriculum and to provide material that reflects the boys’ hobbies and interests. We also have the famous P & G Wells book shop just next door where many families enjoy visits from famous children’s authors and workshops.
POETRY RECITAL AND SPEECH COMPETITION
Boys take part in our annual poetry recital, for which they learn a poem and recite it from memory. Older boys also enter our annual speech competition, competing to engage and enthuse audiences, delivering speeches on a topic of their own choice that they have researched and written themselves. The finals of both competitions are judged by an external adjudicator and always well attended by parents.

FRENCH
More than je m’appelle
le programme d’études français
Boys are encouraged to read, listen and engage with authentic French, developing both enjoyment of the language and the ability to hold conversations with native speakers. A strong balance is maintained between grammar and spoken confidence, with boys encouraged to take risks in both writing and speaking. Learning is supported through songs, games, role-play and enrichment activities such as a French film club.
We use a bespoke curriculum, drawing on the Expo scheme, with pupils working ahead of national levels. By Year 8, most grammar is covered, preparing boys for senior school and future study.
At the top of the school, advanced work develops higher-level skills, including translation, discussion and complex grammar through engaging texts. Native speakers are supported with differentiated work and opportunities to further develop their skills, including informal French-speaking events.
There’s a real focus on a fully rounded education for the boys. There’s not just music, not just sport and not just academic focus – it’s really everything. And that’s important.
SPECIALIST LANGUAGE PRACTICE IN YEAR 8
The French curriculum is further enhanced in Year 8 by a weekly intervention from a specialist language teacher. The boys will work individually or in small groups to sharpen and enhance their speaking and grammatical skills. This further reinforces the notion that language is often a communication tool used on a smaller scale. Everyone gets to make progress at their own rate and, like learning any language, often it is the mistakes that we make which help us learn the most effectively.
